objectives: Read a controlled short /o/ passage accurately.
Sequence key events in the order stated.
Identify details and main idea using text evidence.
Monitor short /o/ decoding while reading connected text.
concepts: Connected reading combines accurate decoding with meaning monitoring.
Sequence depends on the order of events in the text.
Evidence should come from the passage rather than memory or guessing.

definitions.definition: The order in which events happen.
The central meaning of a short passage.
Information in the passage that supports an answer.

workedExamples: dog read as dag → compare the middle vowel and decode again.
commonMistakes: Guessing a word from its first letter.

basic: Read the passage and identify events.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why passage evidence is stronger than a guess.
mixedReview: Decode, sequence and answer passage questions.

weakTopicRevision: Reread each event and point to its position in the passage.

activities.name: Event sequencing
steps: Place events first, next and last.

outcomes: Learner reads the controlled short /o/ passage with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner sequences key events with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner retrieves stated details using text evidence.
Learner identifies the main idea of a short controlled passage.

questions.question: Who is the main person in the passage?
Where does Tom put the mop?
Which event happens first?
options: Tom puts the mop on a log.

questions.question: Which event happens next after Tom sees the dog?
What is the passage mainly about?
options: Tom using a mop and meeting a dog

questions.question: Which word shows where the mop is?
What evidence shows Tom met the dog?
options: The passage says Tom sees and pats the dog.
The title says Tom has a mop.

questions.question: Which sequence is correct?
options: has mop → sees dog → pats dog
pats dog → has mop → sees dog
sees dog → has mop → pats dog
has mop → pats dog → sees dog

questions.question: Why should the learner reread the passage?
options: To check decoding, event order and meaning

questions.question: If “dog” is read as “dag,” what should the learner check?
options: The middle vowel o versus a

questions.question: What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Read a controlled short /o/ passage and explain sequence and details
